result.summary:
Independently validated docs/agents/test-specs/REQ-021.md (branch feature/WF02-REQ-021, commit bc1a450) against docs/agents/design/REQ-021.md (AC1-AC4, especially section 2.3's tie-break rule), handoffs/WF02-REQ-021/step-03-test-designer.json, and the real implementation (apps/bot/src/domain/registration.ts's getWaitlistPosition, apps/bot/src/handlers/registration.ts's composeRegistrationReply, apps/bot/src/i18n/en.ts's registration catalog, apps/bot/src/db/schema.ts's registrations/chapters/users tables). Read the spec file itself in full, not TEST-DESIGNER's result.summary.

What checked out correctly (re-derived myself against the real code, not trusted from the spec's own prose):

1. getWaitlistPosition's real body (apps/bot/src/domain/registration.ts lines 228-272) matches the spec's description of the query exactly: one SELECT...LIMIT 1 for the target row's created_at/admission, null on no-row-found and on non-waitlisted admission, then one count-ahead query with `or(lt(createdAt, target.createdAt), and(eq(createdAt, target.createdAt), lt(id, registrationId)))` -- byte-for-byte the tie-break rule AC2b's fixture is built to exercise, plus 1 for the 1-based position. No discrepancy between design section 2.3, the real code, and what the spec asserts.
2. Every quoted catalog string cross-checked verbatim against the real apps/bot/src/i18n/en.ts registration block: confirmedPrefix "You're in!", whatNext "What happens next: you'll get a check-in code closer to the event.", waitlistedPrefix "You're on the waitlist for:", waitlistedPositionPrefix "Your position:", waitlistedWhatNext "What happens next: you'll move up automatically as seats open." -- AC1's claimed five-line composed reply ("You're on the waitlist for:\nAC1 Event\n<dateTimeText>\nYour position: 1\nWhat happens next: you'll move up automatically as seats open.") matches exactly, no invented copy. The real composeRegistrationReply (handlers/registration.ts lines 123-133) builds the waitlisted-branch lines in exactly the claimed order (prefix, title, dateTime, then the position line only if non-null, then waitlistedWhatNext), confirming AC1's ordering assertion.
3. AC2a's before-flip 3-row check plus the explicit assertion that the third row also shifts 3->2 (not just the second, adjacent row) is a genuinely stronger case than an adjacent-only check: since getWaitlistPosition recomputes a fresh count-ahead query with no cache, an implementation with a hidden off-by-one that only patches the immediately-following row (e.g. a bug that decrements a stored value instead of truly recounting) would pass an adjacent-only check but fail this one. Confirmed there is no code path in the real implementation that treats rows differently by distance from the flipped row -- the count-ahead query is identical regardless of which row asks -- so this is real, non-redundant coverage strengthening, not padding.
4. AC4's 8-registration live-dispatch case matches the real handler and decideRegistrationOutcome's unconditional row-8 waitlisted fallback (registration.ts lines 70-73): with capacity=1 and 9 taps, tap 1 is admitted and taps 2-9 are waitlisted with positions 1..8 in order, matching the spec's expected sequence.
5. No mocked/stubbed grammY Context anywhere: AC1 and AC4 dispatch through a real `new Bot(...)` via `bot.handleUpdate()` against the real REGISTER_CALLBACK_PATTERN/makeRegisterCallbackHandler (confirmed these are real exports of handlers/registration.ts). AC2/AC2b/AC2c correctly call getWaitlistPosition directly with no dispatch -- appropriate since design section 0 itself names this as the correct substitute test method for a domain-function property, not a shortcut around dispatch coverage that belongs there.
6. Every case states an explicit failure mode ("Pass conditions: ... is a FAIL", naming the specific wrong observation). No 'TODO' found anywhere in the file.

BLOCKING FAILURE -- AC2b's tie-break fixture is not mechanically runnable as its own instructions require:

AC2b instructs (docs/agents/test-specs/REQ-021.md lines 221-253): construct two waitlisted rows sharing a byte-identical created_at via a standalone script (apps/bot/scratch-verify-req021-ac2.ts) using seedChapter/seedPublishedEvent/seedUser helpers that the spec itself says should reuse "own uuids distinct from registration.db.test.ts's internal counters, e.g. chapter code 'r21a2script'" -- then explicitly requires 're-run the whole script 3 times to confirm the outcome is not order-dependent... the tie-break must depend only on the id comparison, never on insertion or scan order.'

Checked the real schema this fixture writes against: apps/bot/src/db/schema.ts line 54 defines `uniqueIndex("chapters_code_unique").on(table.code)` on the chapters table, and line 94 defines `uniqueIndex("users_tg_id_unique").on(table.tgId)` on the users table. The spec's own literal example chapter code, 'r21a2script', is a single fixed string, not a per-run-varying value -- and this project's own established seedChapter/seedUser pattern (apps/bot/src/domain/registration.db.test.ts lines 54-83) generates codes/tgIds from module-level counters (`chapterSeq`, `tgSeq`) that start from a fixed base value on every fresh process start. Since AC2b's fixture is a standalone script invoked three separate times via `npx tsx scratch-verify-req021-ac2.ts` (three separate Node processes, not three iterations inside one long-lived process), any counter-based or fixed-literal implementation of these helpers will reproduce the identical chapter code (and, following the same construction pattern, identical seeded tgId values) on run 2 and run 3 that run 1 already committed to the database -- causing a real unique-constraint violation (`chapters_code_unique` and/or `users_tg_id_unique`) rather than a clean confirmation of order-independence.

The spec supplies no cleanup step between the 3 required re-runs of this specific script (the Shared Setup's DELETE-cleanup instruction, step 5, is scoped to isolating AC1/AC2/AC3/AC4 from each other via raw-SQL fixtures, not to isolating three successive invocations of the same TS-helper-based script from each other), and it supplies no randomization/uniqueness strategy for the codes and tgIds these helpers would generate on each fresh process start. Making this runnable as literally written requires TEST-RUNNER to invent one of: a DELETE/TRUNCATE step between runs, a randomized or timestamp-suffixed chapter code and tgId, or a shared persistent counter across processes -- none of which the spec states, which is exactly the 'precise enough to run without judgment' bar Step 3b's check (c) tests for. Read literally, the third repetition (and likely the second) fails on a Postgres constraint violation, not on the property AC2b actually intends to test.

This is the exact case this run's own instructions asked me to scrutinize as the most technically tricky part of the spec, and it does not survive that scrutiny: the tie-break logic itself (item 1 above) is correct and the test's intent is sound, but its fixture-construction instructions are not mechanically executable 3 times in a row as written.

Required fix for TEST-DESIGNER (rework, back to Step 3): AC2b (and, for consistency, AC2a/AC2c's shared script, since they run in the same process before AC2b per the spec's own 'same script, continuing with...' structure) must specify one of: (a) an explicit DELETE/cleanup step for the chapter/event/user rows this script creates, run at the start or end of each of the 3 invocations, or (b) a uniqueness strategy for the seeded chapter code and user tgId that is guaranteed distinct across separate process invocations (e.g. `` `r21a2-${Date.now()}-${Math.random().toString(36).slice(2)}` `` for the code and a similarly-varying tgId base), stated explicitly enough that TEST-RUNNER does not have to invent it. Either fix closes the gap; the current spec does neither.

Everything else in the spec (AC1, AC2a, AC2c, AC3, AC4, AC-catalog, the shared setup's raw-SQL-fixture cases) is precise, judgment-free, grounded in the real implementation, and would fail if violated. This is a single-issue FAIL scoped to AC2b's re-run mechanics, not a wholesale rewrite.

issues.description: AC2b's tie-break fixture (docs/agents/test-specs/REQ-021.md lines 221-253) instructs re-running apps/bot/scratch-verify-req021-ac2.ts three times as three separate `npx tsx` process invocations, but supplies no cleanup step and no cross-run uniqueness strategy for the seeded chapter code / user tgId values its own helpers would generate. apps/bot/src/db/schema.ts enforces `chapters_code_unique` (line 54) and `users_tg_id_unique` (line 94), and the spec's own literal example chapter code ('r21a2script') is a fixed, non-varying string; the project's established seedChapter/seedUser counter pattern (registration.db.test.ts lines 54-83) also restarts from a fixed base on every fresh process start. Run 2 (and 3) of the script will hit a real unique-constraint violation rather than exercising the intended order-independence property. Fix: specify an explicit DELETE/cleanup step between the 3 runs, or a uniqueness strategy for the seeded code/tgId guaranteed distinct across separate process invocations (e.g. a timestamp- or random-suffixed value), stated precisely enough that TEST-RUNNER need not invent it.

result.next_action: Rework TEST-DESIGNER (Step 3) -- fix AC2b's (and its shared script's) re-run mechanics per the MAJOR issue above, then re-route to TEST-DESIGN-VALIDATOR (Step 3b).
